reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Thursdays used to be the hardest day to stay sober. Not Friday — Friday had its own gravity, its own excuse. Thursday was the day I'd start negotiating. One drink after work. A soft landing into the weekend. Thursday was where the slow erosion happened, dressed up as reward.

What I didn't understand then is that a life is mostly Thursdays. It's not the ski trip or the wedding or the big birthday. It's the drive home, the dishes, the text you send a friend because you thought of them. The real question of sobriety isn't whether you can white-knuckle the dramatic moments. It's whether you can show up for the ordinary ones without needing to escape them. Whether you can let a regular Thursday evening just be a Thursday evening — not a problem to be solved with something in a glass.

Durant's line about habit cuts both ways. The drinking was a habit, too. It wasn't a personality, it wasn't a soul-level truth about me — it was a thing I did again and again until it felt like who I was. Sobriety works the same way, in reverse. You show up today. You make dinner. You go to bed at a reasonable hour. And slowly, without ceremony, you become someone who does those things. Someone you can live with.
reflection.meditation: What would it look like to let today just be today — no escape hatch, no reward, no negotiation?

affirmations: I don't need to earn the right to a quiet evening.
Today I am building a life out of ordinary days, and that is enough.
I have agency over what I do next, no matter what came before this moment.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Thursday that doesn't require managing. Grateful for the people who text back, the bed I'll actually sleep in tonight, and the memory of tomorrow morning that will still belong to me. Grateful that the hard years taught me what to notice.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day. That's the whole thing.
